paragraphs.notes: Markush enumeration table continued from the preceding page; the page carries no Tabelle caption and no scaffold drawing, so the shared substituents and the scaffold are fixed on an earlier page. The cells are chemical symbols, not German, so zh and en are the same string. Column headers are printed with superscripts, R1, R2 and R3; the cells print their subscripts, OCH2CF2CF2H, OCH2CF2CF3, OCH2CH2Cl, SO2Me, SO2Et, SOMe, SMe, CF3, and they are transcribed here on the line without formatting. The R1 cell of rows 472 to 475 carries no text at all: each holds a small drawn ring, recorded in drawings, and the bracketed placeholder in this transcription marks where that drawing sits. A small stray ink mark sits in the R3 cell of row 453, well to the right of the printed Br; it looks like scan speckle or a handwritten tick, not a printed character. The table ends part way down the page, the last ruled row being 475, and the rest of the page below the table is blank.

structures.position_in_drawing: 1st and only structure inside the R1 cell of table row Nr. 472
structures.core: a saturated five-membered ring drawn as a pentagon with one ring vertex lettered O at its bottom; no inner double-bond lines, so the ring is fully saturated. This is a tetrahydrofuran (oxolane) ring
substituents: at the ring carbon immediately anticlockwise from the ring O, i.e. the ring carbon adjacent to the ring oxygen on the left-hand side: a bond going up-left to a CH2 vertex, which in turn bonds up-left to an O lettered at the top left of the cell
the left-hand lettered O is the point of attachment of the whole group to the rest of the molecule; its bond to the parent is not drawn, the cell simply ends there
no other substituent is drawn anywhere on the ring
structures.name: (oxolan-2-yl)methoxy, i.e. (tetrahydrofuran-2-yl)methoxy, tetrahydrofurfuryloxy

drawings.notes: This is the R1 value of table row Nr. 472, drawn as a small structure in the cell instead of written as text. Read atom by atom off the drawing: attachment O, then CH2, then a ring carbon that sits next to the ring oxygen, then three further CH2 round to that oxygen, five ring atoms in all with exactly one of them O. The SMILES uses * for the open attachment point at the left-hand O and encodes nothing that is not drawn; the ring carbon bearing the CH2 is a stereocentre but no wedge, hash or stereo label is drawn, so no configuration is recorded. The drawings in rows 472, 473, 474 and 475 are identical to one another.
